steps.check: Image or video directly depicts the promised outcome.

steps.name: Fit the first screen on the brand's real device
steps.does: Fits the PDP's fixed first-screen elements (price, proof, CTA, variant picker, delivery info) on the brand's real mobile device.
steps.check: Fit checked on the brand's actual top device, not a generic simulator.

steps.name: Place controls next to what they change
steps.does: Places every control next to the element it changes, and adds a subscribe-and-save selector for consumable SKUs.
steps.check: Subscribe-and-save only appears on genuinely consumable SKUs.

steps.name: Show delivery ETA and local payment trust
steps.does: Shows delivery ETA or a ZIP code and USPS address serviceability check near the buy box (pincode check where the brand sells in India), and local payment methods beside the FUD reducers.
steps.check: Delivery ETA is computed from real courier data, not a flat promise.

steps.name: Answer the 4 above-the-fold questions
steps.does: Answers what, why this one, why now and why trust you above the fold, with reviews and gallery placed next to the buy box.
steps.check: All 4 questions are answerable from the above-the-fold content alone.

qa: Headline names the outcome, not the category.
First-screen fits on the brand's actual mobile device, tested not assumed.
Every claim in the hero traces to the proof file.
read_point: Founder approves before build; re-scored if the feeding ad or offer changes.
typical_duration: agent: half a day per page.

name: Write persuasion copy, proof and urgency, and keep price claims honest
trigger: on demand | a competitor price change is detected, or a scheduled weekly check
human_role: Page copywriter

steps.name: Write value props in the customer's own words
steps.does: Writes each value prop as a benefit heading with the feature as support, mined from real reviews and tickets.
steps.check: Wording traces to a real review or ticket quote.

steps.name: Show how it works and build an honest comparison
steps.does: Shows how the product works in 3-4 steps ending at the outcome, and builds an honest comparison against 2-3 real alternatives.
steps.check: Every named alternative is real, checkable and currently on the market.

steps.name: Build the FAQ from real tickets
steps.does: Builds the FAQ from that SKU's own tickets and negative reviews, and quantifies claims with a true number wherever one exists.
steps.check: Every FAQ answer traces to a real ticket or review pattern.

steps.name: Map proof to objections and scatter it
steps.does: Maps every testimonial, badge and press quote to the one objection it answers, and scatters proof through the page instead of stacking it once.
steps.check: Every proof element is tagged to one named objection.

steps.name: Add UGC and check review-date clustering
steps.does: Adds phone-shot UGC and a short founder video for trust-led SKUs, and checks review dates for suspicious clustering before trusting them.
steps.check: Any suspicious date cluster is flagged before the reviews are used as proof.

steps.name: Build a post-purchase proof survey
steps.does: Builds a short post-purchase survey to keep collecting proof on purpose instead of waiting for it to arrive.
steps.check: Survey questions map to the objections the page still needs proof for.

steps.name: Write true, risk-framed urgency
steps.does: Uses urgency and scarcity only when true and phrased as risk, never a fake count, and wires a real-time low-stock display to live inventory.
steps.check: Low-stock number matches live inventory, checked at write time.

steps.name: Present the guarantee word-for-word
steps.does: Presents the guarantee as confidence, matched word-for-word to policy, and closes long pages with 2 honest options: leave, or try risk-free.
steps.check: Guarantee wording matches the policy page exactly.

steps.name: Match anchor-price claims to a current source
steps.does: Reads only publicly listed competitor prices already used as signal elsewhere, and matches each PDP anchor-price claim to the specific price it cites.
steps.check: Every comparison claim has a current, dated source attached.
steps.ask_founder_if: a comparison claim has no current, dated source

steps.name: Flag and propose the corrected number
steps.does: Flags a claim as stale the moment the cited competitor price moves enough to make the comparison inaccurate, and proposes the corrected number for a human to approve.
steps.check: No comparison copy changes without human approval.

qa: No urgency or scarcity claim without a true, current basis.
Guarantee copy matches policy word-for-word.
No comparison claim ships without a current, dated competitor source.
read_point: Before page publish (feeds the QA Gate); competitor price check runs weekly.
typical_duration: agent: half a day for a full copy pass; price watch: 15 minutes weekly.

name: Remove friction, QA pages mobile-first and audit accessibility
trigger: on demand | event: before any page launch | quarterly
human_role: Page friction, mobile and accessibility QA lead
inputs_required: key templates (home, PDP, collection, cart, checkout)

steps.name: Strip navigation on single-offer pages
steps.does: Strips navigation to logo, cart and one CTA on single-offer campaign pages.
steps.check: No competing link remains on a single-offer page.

steps.name: Open a cart drawer, not a reload
steps.does: Opens a cart drawer on add-to-cart instead of reloading, and fires pop-ups only on real intent signals, never in the first 3-5 seconds.
steps.check: Pop-up timing tested against an intent signal, not a flat timer.

steps.name: Fix dead controls and remove unused promo boxes
steps.does: Fixes or removes false affordances and dead controls, and removes the cart discount-code box when no promotion is live.
steps.check: Every visible control does something when clicked, tested live.

steps.name: Repair blockers and stage form fields
steps.does: Repairs popups, chat widgets or cookie bars covering add-to-cart, and reveals extra form fields only after the first is filled.
steps.check: Add-to-cart never visually obstructed on a real device screenshot.

steps.name: Build and review every page mobile-first
steps.does: Builds and reviews every page mobile-first, on the brand's own real device split, checking every screen width in responsive mode.
steps.check: Reviewed on the brand's real device split, not a generic phone size.

steps.name: Pin the CTA and never hide content in a carousel
steps.does: Pins the PDP CTA on mobile with live price without covering the variant selector, and never hides reviews or content behind a mobile-only carousel.
steps.check: No content that appears on desktop is hidden behind a carousel on mobile.

steps.name: Cap mobile forms and prioritize mobile effort
steps.does: Cuts mobile forms to 4 fields or fewer with visible labels, and puts about 90% of CRO effort on mobile.
steps.check: No mobile form exceeds 4 fields without a stated reason.

steps.name: Run an automated WCAG scan
steps.does: Runs an automated WCAG scan on home, PDP, collection, cart and checkout templates.
steps.check: All 5 key templates scanned, not just the homepage.

steps.name: Manually test with keyboard and screen reader
steps.does: Manually tests forms, navigation and dynamic states with a keyboard and a screen reader, separating real failures from automated false positives.
steps.check: Manual pass included, not the automated scan alone.

steps.name: Scope remediation to the theme codebase
steps.does: Closes cookie-consent and data-privacy gaps alongside accessibility ones, and scopes every remediation to the theme codebase so fixes survive updates.
steps.check: Remediation lives in the theme codebase, re-scanned after the next theme change.

qa: Every friction fix tested live, not assumed from a screenshot.
Mobile QA run on the brand's own device split, not a generic phone.
Accessibility remediation lives in the theme codebase, re-scanned after the next theme change.
read_point: Before every page launch; accessibility re-audited quarterly and after any theme change.
typical_duration: agent: half a day for friction/mobile QA; accessibility: 1 day including manual testing.

name: Run the advertorial research and drafting pipeline
human_role: Advertorial writer

steps.name: Gather the full research base
steps.does: Gathers reviews, tickets, the competitor set and prior ad performance into one research base before drafting a word.
steps.check: Research base compiled before any copy is written.

steps.name: Rank candidate pains
steps.does: Ranks candidate pains by urgency, scale and relevance to this SKU.
steps.check: Pains are ranked, not just listed.

steps.name: Test the big idea's uniqueness
steps.does: Tests the big idea against the competitor set before committing to it.
steps.check: Big idea checked against every real competitor claim it might overlap.
steps.ask_founder_if: the big idea overlaps closely with a live competitor claim

steps.name: Name the mechanism honestly
steps.does: Names the mechanism honestly with a causal chain a skeptical reader could check.
steps.check: The causal chain is checkable, not a black-box claim.

steps.name: Order in the proven 14-block sequence
steps.does: Orders the advertorial in the proven 14-block sequence.
steps.check: All 14 blocks present in sequence.

steps.name: Write the why-nothing-else-worked block
steps.does: Writes a why-nothing-else-worked block naming real alternatives, not straw men.
steps.check: Every named alternative genuinely exists and is fairly described.

steps.name: Draft with AI, then scrub every fact
steps.does: Drafts with AI from the research base, then scrubs every invented fact by hand against the brand record.
steps.check: Every factual claim traces to the research base, none invented.

steps.name: Run a structured tighten pass
steps.does: Runs a structured tighten pass (cut, don't add) before handing to design.
steps.check: Draft is shorter after the tighten pass, not longer.

steps.name: Run the compliance claims check
steps.does: Runs the compliance claims check before this leaves Site's hands.
steps.check: No forbidden-tier claim reaches the design handoff.

qa: No invented spokesperson, testimonial or study anywhere in the draft.
Every alternative named in the why-nothing-else-worked block is real.
Disclosure label present if required by the channel.
read_point: Founder reviews the draft before it goes to design and paid traffic.
typical_duration: agent: 1 day research plus drafting; human: review and sign-off, same day.

name: Design, build and route a quiz funnel
human_role: Quiz funnel builder

steps.name: Cut questions with no clear job
steps.does: Cuts every candidate question that has no clear job in routing or personalizing the result.
steps.check: Every remaining question can be justified by its downstream use.

steps.name: Open with the least invasive question
steps.does: Opens with the least invasive, most important question, and starts length at 8-12 questions total.
steps.check: Question count starts in the 8-12 range.

steps.name: Test the first 3 hook questions
steps.does: Tests the first 3 hook questions before building the rest of the flow.
steps.check: Hook questions tested separately before the full build.

steps.name: Insert real information screens
steps.does: Inserts a real information screen about every 3-5 questions, never a filler screen.
steps.check: Every info screen carries real, useful content.

steps.name: Build the results page from real answers
steps.does: Builds the results page to show the shopper's own answers reflected back, with exactly one CTA.
steps.check: Results page content changes based on the shopper's actual answers.

steps.name: Route each answer to its offer
steps.does: Routes each answer combination to its matching page or offer.
steps.check: No answer combination is left without a mapped destination.

steps.name: Track completion and purchase together
steps.does: Wires tracking so completion rate and downstream purchase are both measured, and judges the quiz on both together.
steps.check: Both metrics are tracked, not completion alone.

steps.name: QA every branching path
steps.does: QAs the branching logic end to end for every realistic answer path.
steps.check: Every realistic path tested at least once.

qa: No dead-end branch with no matching offer.
Completion rate and purchase rate both tracked, not just completion.
No question included without a clear job.
read_point: Founder reviews the full spec before build; completion and purchase rates read 2 weeks after launch.
typical_duration: agent: 1 day for spec; build: 2-4 days depending on the quiz app.

name: Build the sales-page, order-page and post-purchase upsell funnel
human_role: Funnel page builder

steps.name: Build the sales page's 8 must-haves
steps.does: Builds the sales page with its 8 must-haves, from a scored headline to a credibility section.
steps.check: All 8 must-haves present and each traceable to a real brand fact.

steps.name: Let copy and proof carry the sale
steps.does: Lets copy and proof carry the sale; design removes friction only, it never replaces an argument.
steps.check: No design element is asked to substitute for a missing argument.

steps.name: Build a low-friction order page with a real bump
steps.does: Builds a low-friction order page with obviously labelled fields and a real order bump, not a generic one.
steps.check: Order bump matches what a buyer of this product would actually want.

steps.name: Use a soft first ask for cold store traffic
steps.does: Uses a soft first ask for cold traffic arriving at a store rather than a hard sales page.
steps.check: Cold-traffic variant confirmed softer than the warm-traffic version.

steps.name: Design the upsell for peak emotion
steps.does: Designs a post-purchase upsell timed at peak post-purchase emotion.
steps.check: Upsell placement matches the moment right after order confirmation.

steps.name: Price the upsell by contribution
steps.does: Prices the upsell by contribution per buyer, not by take rate alone.
steps.check: Price is computed from real contribution margin, in code.

steps.name: Pick the upsell by more-of-same or next-problem logic
steps.does: Picks the upsell by more-of-same or next-problem logic, matched to what was just bought.
steps.check: Upsell logically follows from the purchased item, not a generic bestseller.

steps.name: QA the full path as a real buyer
steps.does: QAs the full sales-to-order-to-upsell path as a real buyer would experience it.
steps.check: Full path completed end to end in a real test purchase.

qa: Upsell priced from real contribution margin, computed in code.
Order bump matches what a buyer of this product would actually want.
Full path QA'd end to end before launch.
read_point: Founder gate before launch; contribution-per-buyer checked again after the first 2 weeks of orders.
typical_duration: agent: 1-2 days for the full spec.

name: Run the CRO test lifecycle: design, launch, read, roll out and protect
trigger: on demand | event: before test launch | event: test reaches read point | quarterly
human_role: CRO analyst
inputs_required: registry: prior test results on this brand

steps.name: Check the traffic gate
steps.does: Checks the traffic gate: below the sample-size threshold, plans a bigger change instead of running more small tests.
steps.check: Traffic gate check happens before any test is designed, not after it underperforms.

steps.name: Size the test from the minimum detectable effect
steps.does: Sizes the test from the minimum detectable effect, stated as orders per variant, and computes runtime from arms x sample / weekly traffic, at least 2 full weeks covering each weekday twice.
steps.check: Sample size is stated as orders per variant, never a flat magic number.

steps.name: Set the stopping rule before launch
steps.does: Picks a stopping rule before launch and never peeks outside planned looks; randomizes by user with sticky bucketing and isolates returning-visitor traffic.
steps.check: Stopping rule is written down before the test goes live.

steps.name: QA the test on real devices
steps.does: QAs the test 2-3 times on real devices, confirms tracking fires in both arms, and checks for flicker on a slow connection.
steps.check: Tracking confirmed firing in both arms before launch.

steps.name: Check the promo calendar and run an A/A if needed
steps.does: Checks the promo calendar for overlap, and runs an A/A test when starting a new programme or switching tools.
steps.check: No test launches into an unnoticed promo overlap.
steps.ask_founder_if: a promo overlaps the planned test window

steps.name: Count conversions on a confirmation event
steps.does: At the read point, counts conversions on a confirmation event, never clicks, and never calls a test on one good or bad day.
steps.check: Conversion counted on a real confirmation event, not a click proxy.

steps.name: Check SRM, novelty and device splits
steps.does: Checks sample ratio mismatch, novelty/primacy with a daily plot, and the mobile-only and desktop-only splits before trusting the average.
steps.check: SRM checked and cleared before any result is trusted.

steps.name: Decide from the interval and business value
steps.does: Applies Twyman's law to any surprising win, and decides from the confidence interval and business value together, never p<0.05 alone.
steps.check: Decision cites both the interval and the business value, not a p-value alone.

steps.name: Ship the winner and re-verify
steps.does: Ships the winner as the new control, re-verifies it with fresh recordings and funnel data after shipping, and runs an LTV/returns check before scaling any angle- or claim-driven win.
steps.check: Re-verification happens after shipping, not assumed from the test result alone.

steps.name: Maintain the live-winner register
steps.does: Keeps a live-winner register and re-checks quarterly that every shipped winner is still live, setting founder expectations at a 10-20% win rate for PDP/cart/checkout tests.
steps.check: Every past winner is re-checked live at least once a quarter.

steps.name: Report programme value from a holdout
steps.does: When measuring a feature, popup or the whole programme, reports value from a holdout instead of its own engagement metric or the sum of test lifts.
steps.check: Programme value is never reported as the sum of individual test lifts.

steps.name: State and challenge the identifying assumption
steps.does: States and challenges the identifying assumption before trusting any causal method, and checks the traffic gate before choosing a holdout design.
steps.check: The identifying assumption is written down and challenged, not assumed.

steps.name: Steady noisy revenue tests
steps.does: Turns on CUPED only for returning, identified users, and winsorizes outlier orders or uses a proportion metric to steady a noisy revenue test.
steps.check: A noisy revenue metric is steadied with a named technique, not ignored.

steps.name: Log the full chain to the registry
steps.does: Logs the full test-to-result-to-protection chain to the registry for the next backlog cycle.
steps.check: Every test's full lifecycle is retrievable from the registry.

qa: No verdict from a p-value alone.
No peeking outside the planned looks.
A shipped winner re-verified quarterly, not assumed permanent.
Holdout design states its identifying assumption in writing.
read_point: At the pre-set read point (never earlier); quarterly for winner protection and holdout measurement.
typical_duration: agent: design and QA, half a day; test runtime: 2+ weeks; read and rollout, half a day.

name: Optimize on-site search and build visual search
trigger: on demand | on-site search bottleneck diagnosed and the catalogue is visually distinct enough to benefit
human_role: Search and discovery optimizer

steps.name: Fill filter fields and turn filters on
steps.does: Fills every field a filter needs and turns on search and discovery filters wired to real product fields.
steps.check: Every filter tested returns matching products live.

steps.name: Add predictive text and synonyms
steps.does: Improves search with predictive text and synonym matching.
steps.check: A misspelled or synonym query still returns the right product.

steps.name: Audit search as its own funnel
steps.does: Audits search as its own funnel: query volume, no-results rate, and autocomplete lag treated as an everyday interactivity issue.
steps.check: No-results rate is tracked as its own number, not folded into overall bounce rate.

steps.name: Build and maintain the visual similarity index
steps.does: Embeds every live product's real photos once and keeps the similarity index current as the catalogue changes.
steps.check: Index refresh runs whenever the catalogue changes, not on a stale one-time build.

steps.name: Return real SKUs from an uploaded photo
steps.does: Accepts a shopper-uploaded photo, embeds it the same way, and returns the nearest real SKUs, never a generated or redrawn product.
steps.check: Every returned result is a real, current SKU photo.

steps.name: Cap claims and fall back cleanly
steps.does: Caps the feature to product discovery only, never claims a visual match is exact, and falls back cleanly to text search when no close match exists.
steps.check: No visual match is ever labelled 'exact'.
steps.ask_founder_if: the catalogue is not visually distinct enough to expect a real lift

steps.name: Protect uploaded shopper photos
steps.does: Keeps uploaded shopper photos private and short-lived, never stored as training or competitor data.
steps.check: No uploaded shopper photo persists past the session.

qa: Every filter tested to confirm it returns matching products live.
Visual search never claims an exact match.
No shopper-uploaded photo retained beyond the session.
read_point: Search funnel numbers reviewed monthly; visual search usage reviewed after the first month live.
typical_duration: agent: 1 day for search audit; visual search build: several days, external model dependent.

name: Design on-site personalization and real-time computed offers
trigger: on demand | a PDP has enough session volume and an unresolved add-to-cart drop-off | an exit-intent offer is underperforming
human_role: Personalization and CRO data designer
inputs_required: click-map or session-replay data per PDP

steps.name: Show the shopper's own answers back
steps.does: Shows the shopper's own quiz answers as a personalized progress visual, and recommends a starter pack size from quiz or consumption answers.
steps.check: Every personalized element is sourced from that shopper's own real answers.

steps.name: Match imagery to the selected variant
steps.does: Updates the product image to match the selected variant, and branches the post-quiz email sequence by the shopper's own answers.
steps.check: Image updates correctly for every variant option in a live test.

steps.name: Layer real-time intent signals honestly
steps.does: Layers real-time intent signals into reassurance copy, not only past-browsing history, and tailors PDP facts for AI-referred visitors so they do not re-browse.
steps.check: No personalization rule invents a signal the site does not actually have.

steps.name: Pull real zoom and dwell data
steps.does: Pulls per-image zoom, dwell and skip events from the site's own click-map or session-replay data, never a generic benchmark.
steps.check: Data pulled is this PDP's own, not an industry benchmark.

steps.name: Rank images by real attention
steps.does: Ranks the existing image set by which images hold attention longest before a scroll-away or an add-to-cart.
steps.check: Ranking is computed from real events, not a stylistic guess.

steps.name: Propose the re-sequenced gallery for approval
steps.does: Proposes a re-sequenced gallery order with the reasoning shown per swap, flagging when session volume is too thin to trust the ranking.
steps.check: Proposal goes to the founder gate, never ships automatically.
steps.ask_founder_if: session volume on this SKU is too thin to trust a ranking

steps.name: Read real cost data at the moment of exit intent
steps.does: Reads landed cost, shipping cost and any already-applied promo for the exact cart at the moment of exit intent.
steps.check: Cost inputs read at the moment of the cart, not a stale average.

steps.name: Compute the discount ceiling in code
steps.does: Computes, in code, the maximum discount that cart can take and still clear the founder's margin floor; never lets the model estimate the number.
steps.check: The number is produced by code from real cost data, never a model guess.

steps.name: Show the ceiling logic and fail safe
steps.does: Shows the founder the ceiling logic before turning the offer live, and falls back to no discount, not a guessed one, when a cost input is missing.
steps.check: Missing-cost carts get no discount, never a guessed one.

qa: Every personalization rule sourced from real shopper data, never invented.
Discount ceiling always computed in code from real cost data, never guessed.
Image re-sequencing proposal goes to the founder gate, never ships automatically.
read_point: Founder gate before any rule or offer goes live; re-checked when session volume or margin floor changes.
typical_duration: agent: half a day per feature; discount ceiling logic is reusable once built.

name: Design reviews and UGC display strategy
human_role: Reviews and proof strategist

steps.name: Pick a reviews app and request past reviews
steps.does: Picks a reviews app and requests reviews from past customers before launch if none exist yet.
steps.check: A real request has gone out to past customers, not just the app installed.

steps.name: Decide the verified-purchase policy
steps.does: Decides deliberately whether reviews require a verified purchase, and documents the reason.
steps.check: The decision and its reason are written down, not left implicit.

steps.name: Build volume, then shift sort order
steps.does: Builds review volume first below 100 reviews per product, then shifts sort order to relevance and media-first once past that.
steps.check: Sort order strategy matches the product's actual review count.

steps.name: Check for suspicious date clustering
steps.does: Checks review dates for suspicious clustering before trusting a spike as real.
steps.check: Any suspicious cluster is flagged before the reviews are used as proof.

steps.name: Show repeat-buyer reviews as continuity proof
steps.does: Shows reviews from repeat buyers as continuity proof specifically for consumable products.
steps.check: Repeat-buyer status is verified, not assumed from review text.

steps.name: Confirm the request automation is sending
steps.does: Confirms review-request automation is actually sending by checking a real recent order's timeline.
steps.check: A real order's timeline shows the review request actually fired.

qa: Verified-purchase policy stated and consistent, not ad hoc.
A suspicious review-date cluster is checked before it is trusted as proof.
Review-request automation confirmed sending on a real order.
read_point: Reviewed quarterly alongside the accessibility and hygiene cadence.
typical_duration: agent: half a day.

name: Configure checkout payment methods and address validation, with a WhatsApp buy flow as a market option
trigger: checkout payment mix, failed-delivery rate or chargeback rate identified as a bottleneck in the metric contract | India market option: COD share and RTO rate, or COD/trust-driven checkout hesitation, diagnosed as a bottleneck
human_role: Checkout and payments lead; India market option: India operations lead for COD and WhatsApp
inputs_required: brand's historical chargeback and failed-delivery data
India market option, null for US: courier serviceability API
India market option, null for US: WhatsApp business API access
India market option, null for US: brand's historical RTO data

steps.name: Enable checkout payment methods
steps.does: Enables Shop Pay, PayPal, Apple Pay and a BNPL option (Affirm, Klarna or Afterpay) at checkout.
steps.check: Payment badges and BNPL installment estimate render correctly at checkout.

steps.name: Validate the shipping address against USPS
steps.does: Validates the shipping address against USPS before the order is placed, catching a bad ZIP code or an undeliverable address before it ships.
steps.check: A bad or undeliverable address is caught before checkout completes, not after.

steps.name: Screen orders for fraud signals
steps.does: Screens orders for fraud signals (mismatched billing and shipping, high-risk card BIN, order velocity) and routes flagged orders for manual review.
steps.check: A flagged order reaches a manual review queue, not an auto-approval.

steps.name: Replace tracking with a branded page
steps.does: Replaces the generic carrier tracking link with a branded tracking page that also carries post-purchase upsell content.
steps.check: Tracking page renders correctly on the brand's own domain.

steps.name: Pass a risk score to fulfilment
steps.does: Passes a buyer risk score (first order, high order value, prior chargeback or return-to-sender history, or in India prior RTO history) to the fulfilment system for a manual check, without running carrier-side exception handling itself.
steps.check: Risk score reaches the fulfilment system without Site running the carrier-side process.

steps.name: Build the failed-delivery and chargeback analytics view
steps.does: Builds a failed-delivery and chargeback analytics view by carrier, ZIP code, product and payment method; India market option adds the RTO rate by PIN code.
steps.check: Dashboard breaks the number down by all dimensions, not just an overall rate.

steps.name: India market option, reads null for US: show real-time PIN serviceability
steps.does: Shows real-time PIN code serviceability on the PDP, using the courier or aggregator API, before the shopper adds to cart.
steps.check: Serviceability check reflects the live courier API, not a static list.

steps.name: India market option, reads null for US: add OTP verification on high-value COD
steps.does: Adds address auto-fill and phone OTP verification at checkout for COD orders above a set value.
steps.check: OTP is required only above the set value threshold, confirmed live.

steps.name: India market option, reads null for US: add a visible, sized COD fee
steps.does: Adds a visible COD handling fee as a checkout line item, sized to filter impulse orders without losing genuine buyers.
steps.check: Fee amount is backed by real impulse-order data, not a round guess.

steps.name: India market option, reads null for US: surface a prepaid incentive at the right moment
steps.does: Surfaces a prepaid discount or free-shipping incentive at the exact checkout step where COD is selected.
steps.check: Incentive appears at the COD-selection step, not buried earlier.

steps.name: India market option, reads null for US: trigger a WhatsApp confirmation with auto-cancel
steps.does: Triggers an automated WhatsApp order-confirmation message after COD checkout, with an auto-cancel rule if unconfirmed within a set window.
steps.check: Auto-cancel window is enforced and logged.

steps.name: WhatsApp-commerce market option (India, EU, LATAM), reads null for US: sync the catalogue to WhatsApp
steps.does: Syncs the live catalogue (price, stock, variant) to the brand's WhatsApp Business catalog on a schedule.
steps.check: Catalog sync runs on a schedule and matches the live PDP.

steps.name: WhatsApp-commerce market option (India, EU, LATAM), reads null for US: add the click-to-WhatsApp button
steps.does: Adds a click-to-WhatsApp button on the PDP that pre-fills the exact SKU, variant and a template question, confirmed to appear only where WhatsApp commerce is legal and common.
steps.check: Button appears only in markets where it is confirmed legal and common, never for a US-default brand.

steps.name: WhatsApp-commerce market option (India, EU, LATAM), reads null for US: measure clicks separately and hand off the conversation
steps.does: Measures PDP-to-WhatsApp clicks separately from normal add-to-cart so they are never double-counted, and hands the conversation flow itself to Lifecycle.
steps.check: WhatsApp-originated orders never double-count against add-to-cart.

name: Launch a new paid creative test, start to finish
trigger: an approved card from Propose | on demand
human_role: Performance creative lead running one test from research to the first read
inputs_required: brand brain: voice, audience avatars, claim tiers, product facts
approved idea/card record with bottleneck and expected effect
registry: past creative tests and learnings for this persona and angle
metric contract: hook_rate, cvr_overall, cpa, roas_blended, with freshness stamps
Reference Scout access for competitor and swipe material

steps.name: Pull the objection map and format scan
steps.does: Pulls the brand's existing mined research (voice of customer, owned by the Brand Brain Keeper) plus a fresh check of the account's own last 90 days of ad-level results for which formats currently deliver best (hook rate, hold rate, CPA by format).
inputs: own account ad-level results, last 90 days
steps.output: objection map (each objection quoted and sourced) plus a format scan citing real numbers
steps.check: every objection has a quoted source and a date; every 'format working now' line cites a real metric, not an impression
steps.ask_founder_if: no support inbox or review source is connected for this brand

steps.name: Pull competitor signal for layout and mood
steps.does: Pulls 3 to 8 competitor ad references from the Meta gallery's Competitors tab and the Reference Scout, tagged with why each fits this bottleneck.
steps.output: 3 to 8 tagged competitor references, layout and mood only
steps.check: every reference carries a one-line reason and a 'signal only' tag; no text, logo, product or face is marked for reuse

steps.name: Define the angle and dominant appeal
steps.does: Turns the objection map, format scan and avatar into 2 to 4 candidate angles, each one sentence, one persona, one dominant appeal, one buying question.
steps.output: angle brief: 2 to 4 angles, each with persona, appeal, buying question, awareness stage
steps.check: no angle uses a forbidden-tier claim; each angle names one dominant appeal only

steps.name: Write the test plan
steps.does: Turns the angle brief into a hypothesis, a clean one-persona-per-ad-set structure, a pack size sized to the account's own delivery volume, and a pre-set winner and kill rule for the creative side.
inputs: registry: past test sizes for this brand
steps.output: test brief: hypothesis, pack size, winner rule, kill rule, minimum read window
steps.check: winner and kill rule exist before any script is written; pack size matches this account's real traffic, not a generic default

steps.name: Build the audience spec and hand it to MEDIA
steps.does: Turns the angle's persona into age range, traits, interests and exclusions matched to the avatar record, and hands the spec to the Media buyer specialist as a structured request. CREA does not build or launch the audience itself.
steps.output: audience spec record: age range, traits, exclusions, matched persona id, handed to MEDIA
steps.check: every trait in the spec ties back to a line in the persona record, not a guess
steps.ask_founder_if: the angle targets a persona with no avatar record yet

steps.name: Pick the format and compare format economics
steps.does: Chooses the ad format (static, native platform format, UGC video, founder video, carousel, catalogue) from the product's real education or demo need and the account's own expected profit per ad by format, not ROAS alone.
inputs: product facts: education or demo need
account's own cost-per-asset and format hit-rate history
steps.output: format decision with the profit-per-ad comparison behind it
steps.check: decision cites a number, not a preference

steps.name: Write hooks and scripts or copy per format
steps.does: Writes the hook bank (8 to 20 hooks, graded on 5 criteria) and the format-specific script or static copy structure for each chosen format.
steps.output: hook bank plus a script or copy draft per format
steps.check: no product name or offer in a cold hook; one dominant appeal held throughout

steps.name: Build the creative brief and production or shoot brief
steps.does: Fills the one-page concept brief, then the format-specific production brief (static design brief, UGC or founder-video brief, or catalogue template spec) and generates a first draft image where the format calls for one.
steps.output: concept brief, production brief, and a draft asset (image or script package)
steps.check: destination link matches the offer stated; hook, image and copy share one awareness stage; real product photo used if fit, material or scale matters

steps.name: Run the copy and claim-compliance pass
steps.does: Applies the fixed direct-response copywriting rules (reading level, single idea, proof ranking) and then the brand's claim-tier and platform-policy check on every line.
steps.output: edited copy plus a claim audit table, pass or fail per line
steps.check: reading level under grade 10; no claim from the forbidden tier; no em dash
steps.ask_founder_if: a claim sits at the edge of the site-backed tier

steps.name: Run a feedback and reference round with the Reference Scout
steps.does: Sends the draft brief and asset back through one reference round: checks it against the tagged competitor references for layout and mood fit, and routes it for one internal feedback pass before it reaches a human reviewer.
inputs: past founder feedback notes if any
steps.output: revised brief or asset with a short note on what changed and why
steps.check: no competitor text, logo, product or face was copied in the revision

steps.name: Apply naming and tagging
steps.does: Applies the fixed naming and tagging schema (concept, persona, angle, offer, format, stage, source) to every asset and copy file before it leaves CREA.
steps.check: every asset has a stable id following the current schema

steps.name: Build the launch checklist and hand off to MEDIA
steps.does: Assembles the launch checklist (creative files, copy, audience spec reference, test brief, destination link, tracking check) and hands the full package to the Media buyer specialist for account build and go-live.
steps.output: launch checklist and handoff package to MEDIA
steps.check: every checklist line is checked or has a named blocker; MEDIA confirms receipt

steps.name: Read the first-read numbers
steps.does: At the test brief's minimum read window, pulls the creative-side metrics (hook rate, hold rate, CPA per ad) from the metric contract and compares each ad to the account average and the test's pre-set winner and kill rule.
inputs: metric contract fields at the read window
test brief's winner and kill rule
steps.output: read note: winner, loser or inconclusive, per ad, against the pre-set rule
steps.check: verdict uses the pre-set rule, not a new judgment call; missing metrics show as unavailable, never zero

steps.name: Log the result and close the loop
steps.does: Writes the registry entry for this test (angle, format, hook, result, learning) so the next research pass in step 1 starts from it.
steps.check: entry links back to the original card or idea id

qa: every claim traced to an approved or site-backed tier
no competitor text, logo, product or face reused
reading level under grade 10
real product photo used where accuracy matters
winner and kill rule set before launch
every number came from the metric contract, not estimated
read_point: at the test brief's minimum read window (set in step 4 from the account's own delivery volume, not a fixed default)
typical_duration: agent time: half a day to a day across the pipeline; waiting time: the read window itself, typically 3 to 10 days depending on account volume
subagents: Creative Studio Operator: step 8 image variant generation
Creative Performance Analyst: step 13 read, if a full teardown is warranted

name: Script a founder or authority-led ad

steps.check: every fact in the sheet has a source and a date on file

name: Brief and source a UGC creator, track rights

steps.name: Decide wide or specific brief

steps.does: Writes the concept, the do and don't say list, and the take allowance. Never sends a creator to 'make content' with no concept.

no paid use without a logged rights expiry date

name: Direct a product photo or video shoot

product facts: real dimensions, material, color, fit

steps.check: brief names the exact product variant or SKU being shot, not a generic stand-in

no retouch misrepresents the real product

name: Turn a live product page into a fast first-pass ad variant set

steps.name: Draft a first-pass video or UGC concept

steps.name: Run the copy pass

steps.name: Hand off as a fast-test candidate

real product photo used

name: Diagnose creative fatigue and brief the revival
human_role: Creative performance analyst watching for wear-out

hook bank for the fatigued ad's angle

steps.name: Pull lifecycle metrics

inputs: metric contract: frequency, hold rate, cpa trend
steps.check: every candidate compares to this account's own curve, not a generic industry number

steps.name: Rule out a small-audience-pool cause

steps.name: Diagnose the creative cause

steps.name: Prescribe the cheapest real fix first

steps.does: For audience-pool causes, hands the finding to MEDIA instead of commissioning new creative.

name: Tear down the week's winners and losers

name: Track production cost per asset against the monthly budget
human_role: Creative budget tracker

steps.check: a conflict blocks a new test from starting until resolved

steps.name: Prioritise the next tests to run
steps.does: Ranks the backlog by expected impact, sample size available and dependency order (structure before depth, as offers do).
steps.check: ranking runs in code with score parts visible

steps.name: Specify each test
steps.does: Writes the hypothesis, control and variant, sample split, minimum sample size and pre-registered read window and metric before launch.
steps.check: metric and read window are pre-registered before launch, never chosen after seeing results

steps.name: Set the holdout where relevant
steps.does: For a flow or campaign test measuring incrementality, defines the holdout group size and duration.
steps.check: holdout is large enough to read cleanly, sized in code

steps.name: Hand off the specs to the owning workflow
steps.does: Routes each test's build (flow, campaign, offer, channel) to its own workflow (W04, W06, W18, etc.) with the test spec attached.
steps.check: every spec reaches the workflow that will actually build the variant

steps.name: Log each test to the registry
steps.does: Records id, hypothesis, metric, read point, kill/scale rule before the test goes live.
steps.check: every entry has a metric and a read point that is a contract field

qa: no two running tests confound each other
metric and read window pre-registered before launch
ranking done in code
read_point: per-test, at the pre-registered read window
typical_duration: 2 hours agent time per prioritisation pass

name: Run the monthly lifecycle health review
human_role: lifecycle marketing manager producing the monthly read-out
inputs_required: metric contract: full lifecycle metric chain
registry: this month's tests and their reads

steps.name: Read the full metric chain
steps.does: Pulls list growth, opt-in rate, flow revenue share, campaign revenue share, deliverability, and retention/repeat-rate figures for the month.
steps.check: every field is a contract field; missing ones say unavailable

steps.name: Separate traffic issues from flow issues
steps.does: Checks whether a flow's weak result is caused by low volume entering it (a traffic/segmentation problem) versus a weak flow itself, before diagnosing the flow.
steps.check: a volume problem is never mis-diagnosed as a content problem

steps.name: Pull this month's test reads
steps.does: Reads every registry entry with a read point inside this month.
steps.check: pending reads listed as pending, never as results

steps.name: Diagnose the top 2-3 problems
steps.does: For the weakest points in the metric chain, states the specific cause with evidence, not a general observation.
steps.check: every diagnosis names the exact setting, segment or content issue

steps.name: Recommend the next 2-3 actions
steps.does: Names the specific next workflow to run (a flow rebuild, a segment fix, a deliverability repair) for each diagnosed problem.
steps.check: each recommendation names the workflow id that would execute it

steps.name: Assemble the monthly report
steps.does: Puts the metric chain, diagnoses and recommendations into the report-section shape (what we did, what it did, what is next).
steps.check: matches the report-section output shape

steps.name: Self-QA and post to the founder
steps.does: Runs the QA checklist; this is agent_does since it is a report, not a change.
steps.check: no adjective substitutes for a number

qa: traffic issues separated from flow issues before diagnosing
pending reads never shown as results
every recommendation names an executing workflow
read_point: monthly, compared to the prior month's same report
typical_duration: 2 hours agent time monthly

name: Score churn and lapse risk and route to the right save program
human_role: retention marketing manager reading the order gap and routing saves
inputs_required: order history with per-customer purchase interval
engagement data from the segmentation model

steps.name: Compute each customer's expected next-order gap
steps.does: Reads each customer's own historical purchase interval and flags anyone now past their expected next-order date by a set margin.
steps.check: gap measured against the customer's own cadence, never a flat day count for everyone

steps.name: Pull subscription pause and failed-renewal events
steps.does: Reads any subscription pause, skip or failed-payment event in the window.
steps.check: failed renewals separated from voluntary cancellations

steps.name: Set retry schedule for failed renewals
steps.does: For a failed card renewal, sets the dunning retry cadence by default; for a failed UPI AutoPay or e-mandate renewal (India), sets the retry cadence and the re-authorisation message per current RBI e-mandate rules.
steps.check: retry cadence matches the platform default for a failed card; UPI AutoPay/e-mandate retry timing and re-auth wording match the current RBI rule for India, cited with date

steps.name: Pull unresolved support and engagement decay signals
steps.does: Reads open or recently-escalated tickets and any drop in email/SMS engagement for the same customers.
steps.check: a signal only counts if it is dated within the scoring window

steps.name: Compute the churn-risk score in code
steps.does: Combines order-gap, subscription risk, support and engagement signals into a risk tier (low/medium/high) per customer, all arithmetic in code.
steps.check: no risk score computed or adjusted by the model itself

steps.name: Route each risk tier to its save program
steps.does: Routes low/medium engagement-decay risk to the ordinary win-back flow (W04), delivery-failure risk (return-to-sender for US, RTO for India) to the trust-rebuild win-back variant, and active-subscriber risk to the cancel-flow save offer (W20).
steps.output: routing table by tier and cause
steps.check: a delivery-failure-caused lapse (return-to-sender for US carriers, RTO for India) never routes to a discount-led win-back first

steps.name: Draft the routed message as a live draft
steps.does: For each routed customer or segment, produces the flow entry or one-off draft ready for the founder gate, citing the evidence behind the routing.
steps.check: every draft cites the specific signal that triggered it

steps.name: Report involuntary churn apart from voluntary cancellations
steps.does: Reports the failed-renewal recovery rate separately from the voluntary cancel rate, since blending them hides which lever actually needs fixing.
steps.output: churn report with the two rates kept apart
steps.check: the two rates are never combined into one blended churn number

steps.name: Self-QA and route to the founder gate
steps.does: Runs the QA checklist; every routed save action is founder_gate before it sends.
steps.check: no message sent from this workflow

qa: order gap measured against the customer's own cadence
arithmetic in code only
a delivery-failure-caused lapse (return-to-sender for US carriers, RTO for India) routed to a trust-rebuild message, not a discount
read_point: weekly risk-tier movement; monthly involuntary-churn rate against the prior month
typical_duration: 2 hours agent time weekly

name: Design the post-purchase journey, delivery communication and unboxing experience
human_role: CX lead mapping and designing the after-purchase experience

steps.name: List the post-purchase touchpoints
steps.does: Lists every touchpoint from order confirmation to delivered-and-used (confirmation, shipping update, delivery, unboxing, first use, review request).
steps.check: list covers every real touchpoint the store has, not a generic template

steps.name: Classify each touchpoint by the Kano model
steps.does: Classifies each as basic (must-have, its absence angers), performance (more is better) or delight (unexpected, memorable).
steps.check: every touchpoint has a classification with the reasoning

steps.name: Find the negative peak
steps.does: Reads support tickets and reviews to find the single worst-experienced point in the journey today, with quoted evidence.
steps.check: the peak is evidenced by real quotes, not assumed

steps.name: Design the order-status and delivery communication set
steps.does: Writes the confirmation, shipping and delivery-estimate messages and the branded tracking page content, aimed at cutting WISMO tickets under 5 percent of orders.
steps.output: order-status message set and tracking-page copy
steps.check: delivery-estimate language never promises a date the courier data cannot support

steps.name: Design the unboxing and packaging reveal
steps.does: Designs the layered reveal, insert tiering, and any gift or note, naming this as the journey's main peak to fund, capped to a set share of product cost.
steps.check: spend capped at 2-5 percent of product cost; no falsely-claimed handwritten note

steps.name: Reference competitor unboxing for mood only
steps.does: Pulls competitor unboxing references from the Reference Scout for layout and mood, never copying materials or wording.
steps.check: no competitor text, logo or product reproduced

steps.name: Name the change each map requires
steps.does: States at least one concrete change per touchpoint map, not just a description of the current state.
steps.check: every map names at least one concrete change

steps.name: Assemble the journey and communication brief
steps.does: Puts the touchpoint map, delivery communication set and packaging brief into one document.
steps.check: brief covers order-to-delivered, not just one touchpoint

steps.name: Self-QA and route to the founder gate
steps.does: Runs the QA checklist; packaging spend and message wording changes are founder_gate.
steps.check: no vendor or packaging order placed from this workflow

qa: negative peak evidenced by quotes
delivery estimates match courier data
packaging spend capped to product cost share
read_point: WISMO ticket rate and unboxing-driven UGC volume, read monthly after launch
typical_duration: 1 day agent time; longer if new packaging is sourced

name: Design the returns, exchanges and refund experience
human_role: returns coordinator / CX lead designing the returns flow and policy
inputs_required: support ticket volume tagged as returns

steps.name: Read the current policy and return volume
steps.does: Pulls the live returns policy text and the last quarter's return rate, reason breakdown and refund-cycle time.
steps.check: return rate and reasons come from order/support data, not estimated

steps.name: Check per-market return law
steps.does: Confirms the minimum return window and any mandatory disclosure for each market the brand ships to.
steps.output: legal minimums per market with source and date
steps.check: every legal claim carries a URL and date

steps.name: Set refund speed targets for both legs
steps.does: Sets a target for time-to-pickup and time-to-refund-after-receipt separately, since a returner cares about both.
steps.check: targets are measured against both legs, not one combined number

steps.name: Design the refund-vs-credit choice
steps.does: Designs the choice between cash refund and store credit, including any credit bonus, checked against the brand's margin.
steps.check: any credit bonus is sized against real margin, not an arbitrary number

steps.name: Design the self-service portal rules
steps.does: Sets what a customer can do without contacting support (initiate, choose refund/exchange/credit, print a label) and what needs a human.
steps.check: fraud-flagged or high-value returns route to a human, never full self-service

steps.name: Design failed-delivery and fraud controls
steps.does: Sets the address-risk/fraud check for orders before a return or replacement ships (ZIP/address-validation history for the US); India only: sets the pincode-level RTO risk check and the serial-returner flag for COD orders instead.
steps.output: failed-delivery/fraud control rule (RTO/fraud control rule for India)
steps.check: risk check runs on real address history for the US, or pincode history for India, not a blanket restriction

steps.name: Write the policy text
steps.does: Drafts the customer-facing returns and refund policy page text at a skimmable, honest reading level.
steps.check: claim-check pass; policy visible pre-purchase, not only after checkout

steps.name: Check the returners' repeat-rate gate
steps.does: Confirms any investment in making returns easier is justified by the observed repeat-purchase rate of past returners versus non-returners.
steps.check: investment level matches the measured repeat-rate lift, not assumed goodwill

steps.name: Self-QA and route to the founder gate
steps.does: Runs the QA checklist; every policy or portal change is founder_gate and legal-market-checked.
steps.check: policy text checked against law per market before it ships

outputs: failed-delivery/fraud control rule (RTO/fraud control rule for India)
qa: policy checked against law per market
returns investment gated on returners' repeat rate
failed-delivery/fraud check uses real address history for the US, or pincode history for India
read_point: return rate, refund-cycle time and post-return repeat-purchase rate, read quarterly
typical_duration: 1 day agent time

name: Draft support reply templates, ticket-tagging rules and AI agent governance
human_role: customer support lead / CX manager standing up or refreshing support automation
inputs_required: helpdesk ticket history by contact type

steps.name: Group tickets into contact types
steps.does: Reads a sample of recent tickets and groups them into the common contact types (WISMO, return/exchange, sizing/fit, damaged/defective, payment, cancel/change order, product question, complaint).
steps.check: every high-volume type in the sample has its own bucket, not an 'other' catch-all over 15 percent

steps.name: Draft a reply template per type
steps.does: Writes a template per contact type in the brand's voice, citing current policy for any factual claim.
steps.check: every factual claim in a template traces to the current policy

steps.name: Decide automation scope per type
steps.does: Classifies each type as agent-can-close, agent-can-draft-only, or human-only, keeping human voice for recovery and VIP moments.
steps.check: recovery and VIP-flagged tickets are never agent-can-close

steps.name: Set tagging and routing rules
steps.does: Writes the rule that tags and routes each incoming ticket to the right queue and priority.
steps.check: every contact type maps to exactly one primary tag

steps.name: Write the AI agent's operating procedure
steps.does: For any contact type marked agent-can-close involving money or account changes, writes the exact rule (refund cap, who approves above it, which order states allow a refund) and the identity-verification step required first.
steps.check: every money-moving rule states a hard cap and an approval path above it

steps.name: Set escalation triggers
steps.does: Defines the signals that force escalation to a human: negative sentiment, repeated back-and-forth, an explicit request for a person, or ticket value above a threshold.
steps.check: escalation carries the full conversation history to the human, never a cold restart

steps.name: Replay the agent against real past tickets
steps.does: Tests the drafted operating procedure and templates against a sample of last quarter's real tickets, scoring accuracy and tone before anything goes live.
steps.check: replay uses real past tickets, not synthetic examples

steps.name: Set the kill switch and rollback plan
steps.does: Defines how the AI agent is paused and what reverts if it starts producing wrong answers.
steps.check: rollback restores the prior state in one step

steps.name: Self-QA and route to the founder gate
steps.does: Runs the QA checklist; the operating procedure and any agent-can-close scope are founder_gate before go-live and after every policy change.
steps.check: no AI agent goes live or stays live after a policy change without a fresh replay test

qa: every claim traces to current policy
recovery/VIP tickets stay human
money-moving actions have a hard cap and approval path
replay tested before go-live and after every policy change
read_point: close rate, reopen rate and CSAT by contact type, read monthly; replay score re-checked after every policy change
typical_duration: 1 day agent time for initial setup; 2 hours for a policy-change re-test

name: Run the review collection, response and syndication program
human_role: review platform manager / retention marketing manager

steps.name: Set the review request timing
steps.does: Sets the request to fire about 3 days post-delivery, or hands timing to the reviews app if it already optimises this per product.
steps.check: timing based on delivery date, not order date

steps.name: Draft honest, unfiltered request copy
steps.does: Writes the review request at a skimmable, non-pushy reading level, never implying a reward for a positive review on a destination that forbids incentives.
steps.check: no incentive wording where the destination forbids it

steps.name: Check incentive rules per destination
steps.does: Confirms which review destinations in this request may be incentivised with loyalty points (own site, usually yes) and which may not (Google, most marketplaces, no).
steps.check: a marketplace or Google-bound ask never mentions a reward

steps.name: Draft responses to new reviews
steps.does: Writes an honest, unfiltered response to each new review, especially negative ones, never a templated denial.
steps.check: no manufactured or edited-sounding response

steps.name: Flag defects back to the brand record
steps.does: Routes any review that reveals a real product or fulfilment defect to the brand brain, not just a canned reply.
steps.check: a defect flag names the specific product/fulfilment issue, not a general complaint

steps.name: Rank reviews and UGC for syndication
steps.does: Ranks on-site reviews and photo/video UGC by usefulness (photo attached, specific detail, recency), not star rating alone.
steps.check: ranking uses the stated criteria, not star rating alone

steps.name: Select feed and ad-copy candidates
steps.does: Selects rating/review fields for the product feed and pulls top review quotes as ad copy candidates for the paid-creative specialist, noting the permission basis.
steps.check: quotes are selected and cited, never rewritten

steps.name: Push top reviews into marketplace listings where allowed
steps.does: Where a marketplace allows imported reviews, prepares the content for that listing.
steps.check: only pushed where the marketplace's own terms allow it

steps.name: Self-QA and route
steps.does: Runs the QA checklist; response drafts and any listing/feed write are founder_gate until reviewed.
steps.check: no review is edited, only selected and quoted

no manufactured response
reviews selected and quoted, never rewritten

name: Run VoC surveys and score CX maturity
human_role: CX manager running the standing NPS/CSAT read and the maturity check

steps.name: Start from owned data before surveying
steps.does: Pools open-text answers from closed support tickets and reviews for the quarter before writing a single new survey question.
steps.check: owned data reviewed before any new survey goes out

steps.name: Cluster into recurring themes
steps.does: Clusters the pooled text into named themes with example quotes and a count per theme, flagging any theme new this quarter or growing.
steps.output: theme-clustered report with quotes and counts
steps.check: every theme has at least one quoted example

steps.name: Run or refresh the standing NPS/CSAT survey
steps.does: Sends or checks the standing NPS/CSAT read for the quarter, keeping the same question wording as prior quarters for comparability.
steps.check: wording unchanged from the prior quarter unless a specific reason is logged

steps.name: Add staff input
steps.does: Pulls a short structured input from support/CX staff on what they hear most that a survey or ticket text might miss.
steps.check: staff input is dated and attributed to a role, not anonymous colour

steps.name: Score CX maturity
steps.does: Scores the brand's CX approach as random, intentional or differentiated against a written standard, citing the evidence for the score.
steps.check: score cites specific evidence, not a general impression

steps.name: Check new customer-facing tools against the standard
steps.does: Reviews any customer-facing tool launched this quarter (chatbot, portal, new flow) against the written experience standard.
steps.check: every new tool is checked, none launched without a check on record

steps.name: Route confirmed themes to the owning specialist
steps.does: Sends a confirmed recurring theme to the relevant workflow (returns, support templates, product) rather than letting the report sit unread.
steps.check: every confirmed theme names the workflow it was routed to

steps.name: Assemble and post the quarterly VoC/CX report
steps.does: Puts the theme report, NPS/CSAT trend, staff input and maturity score into one report.
steps.check: matches the report-section output shape

every theme has a quoted example
no new customer-facing tool launched unchecked

name: Design an offer package from margin and AOV
human_role: offers/pricing owner designing a full offer package
inputs_required: discount policy and any founder red line

steps.name: Read margin, AOV and the objection map
steps.does: Pulls landed cost per SKU, the real order-value distribution (not the average) and the buyer's biggest objection from the brand record.
steps.check: AOV distribution used, not the single average figure

steps.name: Write the offer's value proposition
steps.does: Builds the offer as a full package (price, terms, proof, guarantee) scored against the value equation, built around the single biggest objection.
steps.check: the offer answers the stated biggest objection, not a generic benefit

steps.name: Build the margin waterfall
steps.does: Computes the SKU margin waterfall and contribution per order in code for the proposed package.
steps.check: all arithmetic in code; currency conversion applied where relevant

steps.name: Design the bundle and quantity-ladder tiers
steps.does: Maps the product's real use journey into bundle ideas, sizes tiers with a justified reason for each, and pre-selects a middle option, checking every tier clears the contribution floor.
steps.check: at least one full-price entry tier kept; every tier clears the contribution floor

steps.name: Design the gift-with-purchase, if used
steps.does: Chooses a gift that helps the buyer use the core product, sized and placed to lift the tier the brand wants to sell, never framed dishonestly.
steps.check: gift is not more of the same product just bought

steps.name: Design upsell and cross-sell placement
steps.does: Places upsell and cross-sell offers by friction level (cart, checkout, post-purchase), anchored high with a cheaper down-sell, reviewed for margin.
steps.check: placement reviewed against margin and against compliance rules for the platform

steps.name: Cost and write the guarantee
steps.does: Computes the guarantee's net contribution cost from real refund data and writes it in the if-not-X-in-Y-we-will-Z form, activated at delivery, not order date.
steps.check: refund root cause checked before relying on the guarantee to fix a high refund rate

steps.name: Check the whole package against discount policy
steps.does: Runs the assembled package (price, bundle, gift, guarantee) against the discount policy and any founder red line.
steps.check: fails closed and asks the founder if a red line is unclear
steps.ask_founder_if: a founder red line is unclear or missing for this package

steps.name: Set the test plan
steps.does: Names the metric and read window this offer package will be judged on before it launches.
steps.check: metric is a contract field, pre-registered before launch

steps.name: Self-QA and route to the founder gate
steps.does: Runs the QA checklist and sends the full package to the founder for the decision.
steps.output: founder card with the full package
steps.check: no revenue-only or ROAS-only justification accepted

outputs: offer design (output-contract shape: package, objection answered, margin waterfall, contribution, discount-policy check, test plan)
qa: contribution floor cleared on every tier
guarantee cost computed from real refund data
no discount-policy or red-line conflict
test plan pre-registered before launch
read_point: take-rate by tier, contribution per order, and refund rate after guarantee launch, read at the pre-registered window
typical_duration: 1 to 2 days agent time

name: Govern discount policy and price integrity
human_role: offers/pricing owner setting and enforcing the discount rulebook
inputs_required: founder red lines from the decisions log

steps.name: Read discount frequency and depth history
steps.does: Pulls how often and how deep the brand has discounted in the last 6-12 months, by channel and segment.
steps.check: figures come from order/ESP data, not memory

steps.name: Set frequency caps
steps.does: Sets a cap on how often a segment can be offered a discount in a period, so discounting does not train buyers to wait.
steps.check: cap is a specific number and period, not 'occasionally'

steps.name: Set conditionality rules
steps.does: Sets what a discount must require (minimum order value, first-time only, loyalty tier) rather than a blanket site-wide cut.
steps.check: every discount type has a stated condition

steps.name: Set honest framing rules
steps.does: Sets the rule for reference prices and urgency claims: a reference price must be a real prior selling price, and urgency must be real.
steps.check: no fake reference price or fake countdown allowed by the rule

steps.name: Record founder red lines
steps.does: Reads and records any hard limit the founder has already set (a floor price, a channel never discounted, a product never discounted).
steps.check: a red line not on record is treated as unclear, never assumed

steps.name: Write the policy document
steps.does: Assembles frequency caps, conditionality, framing rules and red lines into one governing document every other LIFE workflow checks against.
steps.check: document is specific enough that a pass/fail check needs no judgement call

steps.name: Self-QA and route to the founder gate
steps.does: Runs the QA checklist and sends the policy for founder confirmation before it becomes the standing rule.
steps.check: fails closed - if a rule is ambiguous, the card asks rather than guesses

outputs: discount policy document with frequency, conditionality, framing rules and red lines
qa: every rule is specific enough for a pass/fail check
red lines recorded, not assumed
no fake reference price or urgency allowed
read_point: checked whenever an offer or campaign workflow calls discount-policy-check; policy itself reviewed twice a year
typical_duration: 3 hours agent time

name: Design the subscription offer, perks and cancel flow
human_role: CRM manager / retention marketing manager designing the subscription program

steps.name: Read current subscription economics
steps.does: Pulls active subscriber count, churn rate, pause rate and COGS per subscription cycle.
steps.check: figures scoped to subscription orders only, not blended with one-off orders

steps.name: Size the value proposition against a plain discount
steps.does: Compares the subscription's total value (price, perks, flexibility) against the plain discount it replaces, to confirm the reason to subscribe is stronger than a flat percentage off.
steps.check: comparison shown in real numbers, not just a claim of 'better value'

steps.name: Set cadence flexibility and perk gating
steps.does: Sets how easily a subscriber can change frequency, pause or swap product, and which perks unlock at which tenure or spend.
steps.check: perk gating tied to real use, not an arbitrary tier line

steps.name: Design the four-stage cancel flow
steps.does: Builds the cancel flow as a benefit reminder, an exit-reason survey, a reason-matched alternative (pause, swap, frequency change), then a conditional, costed save offer only if earlier stages fail.
steps.check: cancel is as easy to complete as sign-up; the save offer is conditional, not automatic

steps.name: Cost the save offer
steps.does: Computes the save offer's cost against the subscriber's own order count and value, not one flat offer for everyone.
steps.check: save offer sized in code, matched to the subscriber's own value

steps.name: Cap pause/skip/delay abuse
steps.does: Sets a limit on how many times a subscriber can pause or delay before the cadence auto-adjusts or a human reviews.
steps.check: cap prevents indefinite free pausing without breaking a genuine flexibility need

steps.name: Design non-monetary retention mechanics
steps.does: Adds order streaks, a milestone surprise gift, or a mystery reward as an addition to, not a replacement for, the discount-based save offer.
steps.check: non-monetary mechanic is tested against a discount-only save, not assumed better

steps.name: Set per-stage save-rate tracking
steps.does: Sets the metric to track save rate at each of the four cancel-flow stages, so a weak stage can be rewritten instead of guessed at.
steps.check: each stage has its own named metric

steps.name: Self-QA and route to the founder gate
steps.does: Runs the QA checklist; subscription and cancel-flow design changes are founder_gate.
steps.check: no subscription platform config changed from this workflow

qa: cancel as easy as sign-up
save offer sized to the subscriber's own value
per-stage save rate tracked separately
read_point: per-stage save rate and overall subscriber churn rate, read monthly
typical_duration: 1 day agent time

name: Design referral, partner and payment-term offers
human_role: loyalty/offers program manager designing acquisition-adjacent offers for existing customers

steps.name: Find non-competing partner perks

name: Run the offer testing framework
human_role: offers/pricing owner sequencing and reading offer tests

steps.name: Pull the offer test backlog
steps.does: Reads every proposed offer, bundle, GWP, upsell, guarantee or subscription test not yet run.
steps.check: backlog matches what W18, W20 and W21 have queued

steps.name: Sequence structure before depth
steps.does: Orders tests so structure (does a bundle beat a single SKU at all) is tested before depth (which bundle size wins), one variable at a time.
steps.check: no test changes two variables at once

steps.name: Check dependency order
steps.does: Confirms a test whose prerequisite (e.g. a working discount-policy check) is not yet done ranks below that prerequisite.
steps.check: a dependent test never runs ahead of its prerequisite

steps.name: Pre-register the metric and read window

steps.check: the response date is logged against the statutory deadline

steps.name: Log the request
steps.does: Log every data-subject request and its resolution for audit purposes.
steps.check: the log is queryable by requester and by date

outputs: data-subject request log with responses (India: DPDP request log)
qa: staffing follows the forecast curve
every data-subject request checked against every connected system
deletion or erasure never breaks a legal retention obligation
read_point: monthly for CS capacity; against the statutory deadline for each data-subject request
typical_duration: agent: 1 hour monthly for capacity; 30 to 60 minutes per data-subject request

name: Run the weekly fraud, bot and abuse scan
human_role: the security owner running the weekly scan

steps.name: Rebuild the bot and agent traffic baseline
steps.does: Rebuild the bot and AI-agent traffic baseline by agent, endpoint and intent.
steps.check: the baseline never relies on User-Agent alone

steps.name: Re-score risk tiers
steps.does: Re-score risk tiers per endpoint with continuous tiering, not a one-time label.
steps.check: friction is placed at checkout and account changes, not at browsing

steps.name: Check for new reseller, scalper or card-testing patterns
steps.does: Check for new reseller or scalper patterns and card-testing bursts.
steps.check: a card-testing burst is flagged by its cluster of small failed authorizations

steps.name: Review AVS, CVV and 3DS settings
steps.does: Review AVS/CVV/3DS settings against the false-decline rate.
steps.check: fraud caught is tracked alongside the false-decline rate, never fraud alone

steps.name: Set the chargeback alert threshold
steps.does: Set the chargeback alert threshold below the processor's own flag level.
steps.check: the threshold sits below the processor's own flag point

steps.name: Control step-up verification and payment-refusal triggers
steps.does: Set step-up verification triggers for repeat card-decline or high-risk customers. India-selling brands control COD refusal rate and set prepayment triggers for repeat refusers, the same way, as a market option.
steps.output: payment-refusal control list (India: COD control list)
steps.check: a repeat refuser is flagged by name before the next order, not after

steps.name: Detect return and refund abuse
steps.does: Find wardrobing, serial high-return-rate customers, and refunds issued without a matching return.
steps.check: a flagged customer shows their return rate against the store average

steps.name: Watch domain, DNS and impersonation risk
steps.does: Lock-check the domain registrar account, audit DNS for dangling records, and watch for lookalike domains, counterfeit listings and Safe Browsing flags.
steps.check: a lookalike domain or counterfeit listing is reported with its URL and date found

steps.name: Retest after any recent WAF change
steps.does: If the WAF or bot policy changed this week, retest the baseline against it.
steps.check: the retest confirms the change did not silently block a legitimate agent

steps.name: Build the weekly fix list
steps.does: Roll every finding into one ranked fix list for a human to apply to the WAF or payment settings.
steps.check: every accepted agent keeps scoped authorization, never standing payment access

qa: no rule relies on User-Agent alone
false-decline rate tracked alongside fraud caught
no live WAF or gateway change made by this agent
read_point: weekly, against last week's baseline and fix list
typical_duration: agent: 1.5 to 2 hours
subagents: money-security-scanner runs this workflow on its own weekly clock and hands the fix list to the main agent for QA Gate handoff

name: Run the monthly authentication, web application and backup audit
human_role: the security owner running the monthly technical audit
inputs_required: backup schedule and last restore test

steps.name: Audit login and session design
steps.does: Audit login, session and multi-factor authentication design: 2FA or passkeys for admins, session-cookie attributes, password hashing and rate limiting.
steps.check: every admin account has 2FA or a passkey confirmed, not assumed

steps.name: Check enumeration prevention
steps.does: Check that login and password-reset flows do not leak whether an email exists.
steps.check: the check is tested against the live flow, not the settings page alone

steps.name: Audit storefront and checkout code
steps.does: Audit storefront and checkout code for XSS, injection, CSRF, clickjacking, CORS and postMessage defects.
steps.check: every defect requires parameterised queries or the equivalent fix named exactly

steps.name: Produce the developer fix list
steps.does: Produce a developer fix list from the defect audit.
steps.check: each fix names the exact file or endpoint where possible

steps.name: Run daily versioned backups check
steps.does: Confirm daily versioned backups exist in 3 separated locations with a ransomware-safe copy.
steps.check: a ransomware-safe, offline copy is confirmed, not assumed from the vendor's claim

steps.name: Test restores end to end
steps.does: Test a restore end to end this month, not just confirm the backup exists.
steps.check: the test restores a real file and confirms it opens correctly

steps.name: Maintain the incident runbook
steps.does: Maintain one unified incident runbook covering breach, skimmer and ransomware scenarios.
steps.check: the runbook names who does what in the first hour of each scenario

steps.name: Publish the monthly audit result
steps.does: Publish the auth, web app and backup audit as one ranked fix list.
steps.check: every fix states whether it needs a developer or a founder decision

outputs: web app defect list and developer fix list
backup coverage and restore test result
qa: 2FA confirmed live, not assumed
restore tested end to end, not just scheduled
no code change applied by this agent
read_point: monthly, against last month's fix list
typical_duration: agent: 1.5 to 2.5 hours
subagents: money-security-scanner shares the headless-browser probing across this and the weekly scan

name: Run the quarterly security audit program
human_role: the security owner running the four-pillar quarterly program
inputs_required: staff roster and admin role map

steps.name: Map roles to admin areas
steps.does: Map every staff role to only the admin areas it needs, least-privilege by default.
steps.check: no role has an admin area it does not use

steps.name: Run the full staff access audit
steps.does: Run a full staff access audit with same-day offboarding confirmed for any exits since the last audit.
steps.check: every exited staff member's access is confirmed revoked, not assumed

steps.name: Monitor admin logins
steps.does: Monitor admin logins for new locations or devices since the last audit.
steps.check: a new location or device is flagged even if the login succeeded

steps.name: Confirm GDPR and CCPA exposure
steps.does: Confirm GDPR/CCPA exposure by customer location and publish a privacy policy covering AI-agent interactions with a compliant consent banner.
steps.check: AI-agent interactions are named explicitly in the policy

steps.name: Remove non-payment third-party scripts before consent
steps.does: Remove any non-payment third-party script that fires before consent is given.
